articles.title: TCS Beats Revenue Estimates as AI Business Crosses $2.6 Billion — What NRI Investors Should Know
articles.excerpt: India's largest IT exporter posted 14% revenue growth, restarted hiring after three years, and expanded partnerships with Anthropic and Mistral. The dividend cheque lands July 31.
articles.image_caption: TCS Gitanjali Park campus in Kolkata, one of the company's major technology hubs
articles.nri_angle: TCS is one of the largest H-1B employers and a cornerstone holding for NRI investors. The $2.6B AI revenue run rate, dividend declaration, and hiring restart all directly impact diaspora portfolios and career prospects.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Pour $1 Billion Into Indian Real Estate in Q2 — A 454% Surge That NRIs Should Watch
articles.excerpt: Institutional investment in Indian property hit $2.68 billion in the April-June quarter, with Chennai and Bengaluru overtaking Mumbai as the top targets. Here's what the data means for diaspora buyers.
articles.image_caption: Mumbai's skyline — India's commercial real estate drew $1.88 billion in institutional investment in Q2 2026
articles.nri_angle: NRIs are significant property investors in India under FEMA rules. The surge in foreign institutional capital validates India's real estate thesis, while rupee weakness near 95.4/$ offers diaspora buyers an effective discount on INR-denominated assets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold Hits ₹1.44 Lakh, SGBs Are at a Premium, and New Issuances Are Dead — Here's How NRIs Should Buy Gold Now
articles.excerpt: With 24-carat gold up ₹11,000 in 2026 and Sovereign Gold Bonds no longer being issued, NRI investors need to rethink how they access India's favourite asset class.
articles.image_caption: Gold bars — the metal has climbed ₹11,000 in 2026 to ₹1.44 lakh per 10 grams
articles.nri_angle: Gold remains culturally and financially significant for NRIs. With SGBs effectively closed to new buyers and secondary-market premiums eroding value, diaspora investors need updated strategies for gold allocation across India and the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Pour $1.5 Billion Into Indian Banks in Biggest Buying Spree Since 2025
articles.excerpt: Policy support, cheaper valuations, and easing rate-hike fears are drawing FPIs back to Indian financials after 18 months of record outflows — but oil prices threaten the recovery.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, India's financial capital
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with Indian bank ETFs, HDFC ADRs, and NRE deposits benefit directly from the FPI flow reversal and elimination of capital gains and withholding taxes on foreign investments.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Razorpay to the NSE: Inside India's $51 Billion IPO Pipeline That Could Rewrite Market History
articles.excerpt: With 251 companies in the queue and mega listings from the National Stock Exchange, Razorpay, and Reliance Jio on the horizon, India's second-half IPO wave promises to be its most consequential yet.
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India building in Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors can participate in Indian IPOs through demat accounts linked to NRE/NRO accounts. Razorpay's reverse flip from US to India represents a structural trend bringing diaspora-connected companies to Indian exchanges.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sensex Crashes 1,677 Points as Trump Declares Iran Deal 'Over' — Oil Surges, Rupee Hits One-Month Low
articles.excerpt: Indian markets suffered their worst single-day fall in three months after the US-Iran ceasefire collapsed, sending Brent crude past $79, the rupee to 95.55, and the India VIX up 26 percent — a triple blow for NRI investors watching from abroad.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, home to the Sensex index
articles.nri_angle: India imports 85% of its crude oil — the Iran-driven spike threatens higher inflation, a weaker rupee, and delayed rate cuts, directly impacting NRI remittances, mutual fund returns, and property investment plans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Largest Mutual Fund House Is Going Public — and Abu Dhabi and Singapore's Sovereign Funds Are Already In
articles.excerpt: SBI Funds Management's $1.2 billion IPO kicks off a wave of blockbuster listings that could raise $50 billion in the second half of 2026.
articles.image_caption: State Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors can participate in the SBI Funds IPO through Indian demat accounts; the listing is a proxy for India's mutual fund revolution driven by millions of SIP investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
